vs

full_judgment: 3. The petitioner filed this petition contending that he owns agricultural land in the local area of Barisal Sadar measuring 14.50 decimals land. In 1950 the petitioner had been paying taxes @ Taka 1 (one) per decimal for agricultural land and Taka 7 (Seven) for homestead per annum. The petitioner has 4.50 decimals of agricultural land and 10 decimals of homestead. The land development tax receipts show that the petitioner has paid Taka 74.50 for 5 years (1415 BS-1420 BS) for his 14.50 decimals of land. In 1421 BS (2014) land development tax was revised and enhanced to Taka 7.00 for both agricultural land and homestead. When the petitioner went to pay current tax for his land, he came to know that respondent No. 4 on 30-6-2015 published a circular vide memo No. 31.00.000.044.39.025.15-77(120) dated 30-6-2015 enhancing the land development tax effective from 1-7-20.15 at a flat rate undermining the different nature and pattern of use of land (Annexure B). The petitioner and other affected people in the local area contacted respondent No.4 and requested him to postpone collection of land development tax at the new rate until there is clarification from the Government. Respondent No.5 (Deputy Commissioner, Barisal) advised the petitioner to refer the matter to respondent No.1 for seeking redress on the issue. The petitioner and other affected people of the area formed a temporary organization under the name "বর্ধিত খাজনা প্রত্যাহার কমিটি" and staged public protests. They sent a memorandum to the Hon'ble Minister, Ministry of Land demanding withdrawal of excessive enhancement of land development tax. On 28-3-2016, the petitioner and others held a press conference in the local area demanding withdrawal of enhanced land development tax. On 10-5-2016, the petitioner and others submitted an application (Annexure-E) to the Hon'ble Minister, Ministry of land through respondent No.5 to withdraw the enhanced land development tax which is several times higher than the previous rate. Section 3(1A) (a) of the Land Development Tax Ordinance, 1976 empowers the Government to revise, enhance or reduce the rate of land development tax specified in section 3(1) of the Ordinance which is ultra vires Articles 81, 82 and 83 of the Constitution. Hence this writ petition.
